# 2026-07-26 · Carry settlement currency on the order

Change ID: `settlement-currency`
Created: `2026-07-26T22:46:23+09:00`
Risk: R2

## Problem and intended outcome

Two partners onboarding this quarter settle in currencies other than USD.
Today the currency is implied by the partner and hard-coded at the reporting
layer, which is already wrong for one existing partner and is worked around
by hand each month.

The intended outcome is that settlement currency is stored on the order
itself. The adapter sends it with the payload; reporting reads it from the
row instead of a lookup table.

## Success and non-goals

Success is that reporting derives currency from the order row for every
order, with no hard-coded or partner-implied currency left in the reporting
path.

Not in scope: how amounts are converted for partner-specific rounding rules
(covered by `partner-settlement-rounding`); this change only carries the
currency code alongside the amount.

## Existing responsibilities searched

`src/db/schema.py` owns the orders table shape, so the new
`settlement_currency` column is added there, defaulting to `'USD'`.
`src/api/partner_adapter.py` already owns the settlement payload shape (see
`partner-settlement-rounding`), so it is the place to add the currency field
rather than a new helper. No reporting module exists yet in this codebase;
the read-path change lands when that code is added.

## System and data flow

Order row (`settlement_currency`, defaulted to USD) -> `to_partner_payload`
-> partner settlement API, and separately -> reporting read path (once it
exists) instead of a per-partner lookup table.

## Decisions and trade-offs

See `docs/engineering/decisions/settlement-currency.md`. A per-partner
currency table was rejected: currency is a property of the agreement in
force when the order was placed, not of the partner today, and a table loses
that once an agreement changes.

## Failure, security, and recovery

If the column is missing a currency value, downstream reporting would fall
back to an incorrect assumption; the `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD'` constraint
prevents nulls and keeps existing/historic orders correct, since USD is
correct for every order placed so far. Rollback is dropping the column and
reverting the adapter/reporting changes; no partner-facing contract changes
until the adapter payload change ships.

## Verification evidence

Not yet run for this change; see `.engineering/evidence/settlement-currency.json`.

## Known limits and learning gaps

Per the implementation plan, only the schema column (step 1) has been
started (uncommitted `src/db/schema.py` change). Backfilling existing rows
(step 2), including currency in the adapter payload (step 3), reading it in
reporting (step 4), and removing the hard-coded reporting currency (step 5)
are not started despite the plan noting step 3 as "in progress" -- no
currency field exists yet in `src/api/partner_adapter.py`.

## References

- Proposal: `docs/proposals/settlement-currency.md`
- Implementation plan: `plans/settlement-currency.md`
- ADR: `docs/engineering/decisions/settlement-currency.md`

# 2026-07-26 · Carry settlement currency on the order

Change ID: `settlement-currency`
Created: `2026-07-26T22:46:23+09:00`
Status: Proposed

## Context

Settlement currency is currently implied by the partner and hard-coded at
the reporting layer. This is already wrong for one existing partner and two
more onboarding this quarter settle in non-USD currencies, so the workaround
is done by hand each month.

## Options considered

1. A per-partner currency table, keyed by partner ID.
2. Store the settlement currency on the order row itself.

## Decision

Choose option 2. Currency is a property of the agreement in force when the
order was placed, not of the partner today; a per-partner table loses that
distinction once an agreement changes. The order stores its own
`settlement_currency`, the adapter sends it with the payload, and reporting
reads it from the row instead of a lookup.

## Consequences and reversal

Historic rows are backfilled to USD, which is correct for every order placed
so far. New orders default to `'USD'` unless set otherwise. Reversal is
dropping the `settlement_currency` column and reverting the adapter/reporting
reads back to the partner-implied/hard-coded currency.

## Implementation references

- `src/db/schema.py` (column added, not yet backfilled/committed)

## Supersession

Supersedes: None
Superseded by: None
